catalyst.event: Fed repricing from cuts to hikes on the Hormuz oil supply shock; October FOMC now carries ~64% odds of a 25bp hike
catalyst.action: AMENDMENT to the TLT short already published at 81.87, which the market left behind. Short into strength toward the 20-day SMA rather than chasing the low; do not add below 76.

thesis: The 10-year at 5.11% is the highest since July 2007 and the 30-year at ~5.5% the highest since 2004, and the repricing is not a term-premium story but a policy story: futures now put ~64% on a 25bp October hike and ~48% on December, against an effective funds rate still at 3.88%. TLT closed at 79.42, a 250-day low, with the 20-, 50- and 200-day averages stacked above it at 81.56, 82.35 and 85.71 — every marginal holder of duration bought higher.
key_risk: A Hormuz ceasefire or any credible de-escalation with Iran takes crude back under $90 and the whole inflation impulse with it; long-duration bonds would retrace the move faster than a stop can be honoured, and this is a gap-risk short rather than a grind. (Conviction raised from 3 to 4 on review to match the 3 distinct kinds of evidence listed, per the mechanical rule in config/strategy.md; the lower confidence I have in this idea is expressed in win_probability and position size, not by understating the evidence count.)
counter_argument: Short-duration positioning is already crowded and 5.11% is a level that has historically attracted real money — pensions and insurers buy the long end for liability matching at 5%+, which is precisely why the 2023 push through 5% failed within weeks. The answer is that 2023 had a Fed cutting into a disinflation; this one has a Fed being pushed back toward hiking, so the carry argument for catching the falling bond is materially worse.

catalyst.event: Hormuz crude throughput down to under 2 mbpd from 8-9 mbpd pre-conflict, holding crude above $100 with no de-escalation path
catalyst.action: HOLD the position opened 2026-08-15 with levels unchanged. The 62.00-64.30 zone is still live for anyone not yet filled.

thesis: This is an update to the long opened 2026-08-15 at 63.90, now 62.60. It is held because the divergence that justified it has widened rather than closed: crude is above $100 on a physical supply disruption while XLE still trades below its 20-day average at 64.01. The sector is also leading - XLE is beating SPY by 0.7% over one month and 11.3% over three - so this is not a falling sector being bought for its yield.
key_risk: The entire position is a bet on a shooting war continuing. A US-Iran ceasefire reopens Hormuz and takes crude back through $90 in days, and XLE would give back the 3-month outperformance faster than the 60.80 stop can be worked. There is no company-specific support underneath this, only the geopolitical premium. (Conviction raised from 3 to 4 on review to match the 3 distinct kinds of evidence listed, per the mechanical rule in config/strategy.md; the lower confidence I have in this idea is expressed in win_probability and position size, not by understating the evidence count.)
counter_argument: The strongest case against holding is that crude above $100 is itself the mechanism that ends the trade - it forces demand destruction and a Fed that is already being pushed toward hiking, so the equity market may be correctly refusing to capitalise these prices, which is exactly what XLE trading below its 20-day while crude makes highs looks like. The answer is that the disruption is physical rather than speculative: barrels are not moving, and that does not resolve on a demand signal.
